# HMPFL Week 6 Recap: Lockdown Report

Another week behind bars, another round of inmates fighting for their fantasy freedom. The warden's got the scoreboard posted on the cell block wall, and some of y'all are looking at hard time. Let's run the yard.

## The Tightest Cell Check: ConVicks Survive By a Shiv's Edge

The ConVicks escaped with a 205.75–200.1 nail-biter over OJ's Denver Bronco, winning by just 5.65 points. This one came down to the wire like a last-minute pardon request. Tyler Shough (52.8) and Christian McCaffrey (48.4) combined to bail The ConVicks out of solitary, proving that sometimes you don't need a flashy breakout — you just need your stars to show up for roll call.

## The Yard Massacre: Rice, Rice Baby Runs the Block

If you thought prison justice was brutal, Rice, Rice Baby ✨ just put Glove Don't Fit, Blitz in the infirmary, 259.35 to 183.75 — a 75.6-point beatdown that's the biggest blowout of the week by a mile. James Cook (48.6) led the charge, but this was less "win" and more "full cavity search." Glove Don't Fit, Blitz actually got a monster game out of Kenneth Walker (55.8), the single highest individual score among losers this week, and it still wasn't close. Sometimes you bring a shank to a riot.

## Trevor Lawrence Breaks Out

Big shoutout to DUIiiiiiiii dont know jim, who rode Trevor Lawrence's absurd 60.8-point outburst — the week's top individual score — to a 217.5–206.25 escape from The Massage Boys. Lawrence basically tunneled through the yard wall with a spoon and sprinted to the state line. Malik Nabers (43.0) gave The Massage Boys a fight, but it wasn't enough to stop the breakout.

## Other Notable Headcounts

Smack my Diggs Up handled business against Ruggs, Drugs and TDs, winning by 32.6 behind Drake Maye's 49.8. Steve Ruggs put The Adrian BeatHisSons in the hole, 202.5–167.4, despite Jayden Daniels dropping 47.0 in a losing effort. And Hernandez Hitmen absolutely dominated Josh Allen's Prison Cell, 190.35–133.60, a 56.75-point beating fueled by a two-QB system of C.J. Stroud (53.2) and Kirk Cousins (45.3) — that's some serious double-bunking production.

Stay sharp out there, inmates. Week 7's commissary orders are already being drawn up.
